en.title: ASEAN cross-border dispute resolution: arbitration and enforcement
en.standfirst: Why businesses write SIAC arbitration clauses into ASEAN contracts, how Arb-Med-Arb works, and what the New York Convention does and does not do for enforcement.
en.metaDescription: How to plan dispute resolution for ASEAN contracts: SIAC arbitration, Arb-Med-Arb mediation and enforcing awards under the New York Convention.
en.body:
Planning **ASEAN cross-border dispute resolution** begins before a contract is signed. Businesses need to consider how a disagreement will be resolved and where an eventual decision may need to be enforced.

For companies researching **SIAC arbitration** arrangements, Singapore offers an institutional arbitration option. Understanding **New York Convention enforcement in ASEAN** is equally important when preparing a **B2B contract in Southeast Asia**.

Arbitration can provide an agreed dispute-resolution framework, but it does not guarantee inexpensive proceedings or automatic recovery.

## The risk of local litigation

A cross-border dispute can involve unfamiliar procedures, translation requirements and uncertainty about enforcement.

Assess those issues when negotiating the contract rather than waiting until a payment or performance dispute arises. The appropriate process depends on the transaction, parties and jurisdictions involved.

Domestic courts and arbitration should be assessed against the particular transaction. Likewise, regional generalisations about court reliability or business culture should not replace a transaction-specific assessment.

Consider the likely cost and practical consequences of the chosen process alongside the commercial terms.

## The SIAC option

The Singapore International Arbitration Centre (SIAC) administers commercial arbitration. Parties can agree to use its rules when drafting their contract.

SIAC also works with the Singapore International Mediation Centre (SIMC) through the **Arb-Med-Arb** framework. This combines arbitration with an opportunity to mediate. A settlement reached through that process may be recorded as a consent award, subject to the applicable requirements. [SIMC: Arb-Med-Arb](https://www.simc.com.sg/arb-med-arb)

Mediation depends on agreement and does not guarantee settlement. Arbitration also involves institutional and professional costs that should be considered when selecting the process.

## The New York Convention

The New York Convention provides a framework for recognising and enforcing foreign arbitral awards in contracting states.

It does not mean that a successful party receives payment automatically. Recognition and enforcement may require an application to the relevant court, and the Convention permits refusal on specified grounds, including public-policy grounds. [UNCITRAL: New York Convention guidance](https://uncitral.un.org/sites/uncitral.un.org/files/media-documents/uncitral/en/2016_guide_on_the_convention.pdf)

Enforcement planning should therefore form part of the original contract assessment. A contractual arbitration clause and a favourable award are important stages, but neither eliminates the need to consider the jurisdiction where enforcement will be sought.

## Drafting the contract clause

Use SIAC's current model-clause materials as a starting point for specialist review.

Singapore as the seat and English as the language are options to consider. Those choices should be expressly assessed and recorded rather than assumed from the institution's location.

Also consider whether negotiation or mediation should form part of the agreed process. If a dispute develops, follow the contract's procedural requirements before commencing proceedings.

Consult the [Singapore International Arbitration Centre](https://siac.org.sg/) for its current rules and model clauses. The objective is a clear, workable agreement suited to the transaction.

zh.title: 東協跨境爭議解決：仲裁與執行
zh.standfirst: 為什麼企業在東協合約中納入 SIAC 仲裁條款、Arb-Med-Arb 如何運作，以及《紐約公約》在執行層面能做到與做不到的事。
zh.metaDescription: 如何為東協合約規劃爭議解決機制：SIAC 仲裁、Arb-Med-Arb 調解，以及依《紐約公約》執行仲裁判斷。
zh.body:
**東協跨境爭議解決**的規劃，應在合約簽署之前就開始。企業需要考慮爭議將如何解決，以及最終的裁決可能需要在哪裡執行。

對於研究 **SIAC 仲裁**安排的公司而言，新加坡提供了機構仲裁的選項。在準備**東南亞 B2B 合約**時，了解**《紐約公約》在東協的執行機制**同樣重要。

仲裁可以提供雙方約定的爭議解決框架，但不保證程序費用低廉，也不保證能自動取回款項。

## 當地訴訟的風險

跨境爭議可能涉及不熟悉的程序、翻譯要求，以及執行上的不確定性。

這些問題應在合約談判階段就加以評估，而不是等到付款或履約爭議發生後才處理。合適的程序取決於交易內容、當事人及所涉及的司法管轄區。

國內法院與仲裁都應針對具體交易進行評估。同樣地，對法院可靠性或商業文化的區域性概括，不應取代針對個別交易的評估。

在考量商業條款的同時，也應考慮所選程序可能產生的費用及實際後果。

## SIAC 的選項

新加坡國際仲裁中心（Singapore International Arbitration Centre，SIAC）負責管理商業仲裁。當事人可在起草合約時約定採用其仲裁規則。

SIAC 亦透過 **Arb-Med-Arb**（仲裁、調解、仲裁）框架與新加坡國際調解中心（Singapore International Mediation Centre，SIMC）合作。此框架將仲裁與調解機會結合。透過該程序達成的和解，在符合適用要求的前提下，可以記錄為合意仲裁判斷。[SIMC：Arb-Med-Arb](https://www.simc.com.sg/arb-med-arb)

調解取決於雙方同意，且不保證達成和解。仲裁也涉及機構費用與專業人員費用，在選擇程序時應一併考量。

## 《紐約公約》

《紐約公約》為在締約國承認及執行外國仲裁判斷提供了框架。

這並不表示勝訴方會自動收到款項。承認與執行可能需要向相關法院提出申請，且公約允許法院基於特定理由（包括公共政策理由）拒絕執行。[UNCITRAL：紐約公約指南](https://uncitral.un.org/sites/uncitral.un.org/files/media-documents/uncitral/en/2016_guide_on_the_convention.pdf)

因此，執行規劃應成為最初合約評估的一部分。合約中的仲裁條款與有利的仲裁判斷都是重要的階段，但兩者都不能免除對擬聲請執行所在司法管轄區的考量。

## 起草合約條款

以 SIAC 現行的示範條款資料作為起點，再交由專業人士審閱。

以新加坡為仲裁地、以英文為仲裁語言，是可以考慮的選項。這些選擇應經明確評估並記錄於合約中，而不是因仲裁機構所在地而被視為理所當然。

同時考慮是否應將協商或調解納入約定的程序。若爭議發生，應先依合約的程序要求辦理，再啟動正式程序。

請參閱[新加坡國際仲裁中心](https://siac.org.sg/)的現行規則及示範條款。目標是訂出一份清楚、可行且符合交易需要的協議。
